name: Box of cuvettes
description: A small clear box of square plastic sample cells, each made to the same exact width so a light passes through the same depth of liquid every time.
notes: 112 by 46 mm and 50 mm tall: two rows of seven 12.5 mm cuvettes with frosted grips standing in a white rack, the clear lid hinged up behind and a label with a blue band on the front. Clear plastic draws opaque in the tiles. No quality: the cells only matter to a spectrometer, which has no content yet.

name: Electrolysis kit
description: A copper plate and a steel plate set in an insulated bar, wired to a pair of battery clamps. Clip it to a battery and lower the plates into a liquid to drive a current through it.
notes: Laid flat, 288 by 98 mm: a black bar holding copper and stainless electrodes 30 by 60 mm, red and black leads and two spring battery clamps with copper jaws. electrolysis is a new quality name for crafting that needs a current through a liquid. Running it off a battery has no content field yet. The leads spread the bounding box.

name: Glass prism
description: A clear triangular bar of optical glass that bends light and splits it into its colours.
notes: An equilateral prism 30 mm on a side and 50 mm long, lying on one face. The tiles draw the glass opaque. The bounding box of a triangle is twice its area.

name: Glass desk thermometer
description: A heavy column of solid glass on a round foot, a silver thread of mercury rising in front of a printed scale. It reads the air temperature accurately.
notes: A 150 mm column 40 by 24 mm on a 70 mm foot, a white scale with ticks, a silver mercury thread and bulb. A solid glass desk thermometer rather than a stem thermometer. The tiles draw the glass opaque. temperature_measurement is the quality it brings.

name: Small glass tube
description: A short length of plain glass tubing, open at both ends. A spare part for laboratory glassware.
notes: 100 mm long and 12 mm across with a 2.5 mm wall, lying along x. The tiles draw the glass opaque. The burette and the fractional distillation apparatus ride here, but each is a different shape and weight and would deserve its own model.

name: Dial hygrometer
description: A small plastic dial on a foot whose needle shows how damp the air is, across dry, comfortable and wet bands.
notes: 46 mm across and 14 mm deep in a blue case on a small foot, dial to the front: white face, an arc of ticks, orange, green and blue bands and a black needle. humidity_measurement is a new quality name, after temperature_measurement.

name: Light meter
description: A handheld meter with a white dome over its sensor and a small display that reads how brightly a place is lit.
notes: 140 by 66 mm and 28 mm deep, lying face up: yellow body, dark face, green display, four buttons and a frosted diffuser dome at the far end. light_measurement is a new quality name. Batteries and reading light levels have no content field yet.

name: Box of coarse filter paper
description: A box of fine paper discs for straining solids out of a liquid. This coarser grade holds back more but drains slowly. It is meant to be thrown away, but lasts a while if rinsed.
notes: The model is the round card box of discs a player would find, 125 mm across: the base filled with white discs and the lid beside it with a red grade band and label. filtering is a new quality name for separating solids from a liquid; this coarser grade is filtering 1, below the finer quantitative paper.

name: Box of fine filter paper
description: A box of fine paper discs for straining solids out of a liquid. This grade drains faster and leaves almost nothing behind in the paper, for careful measured work.
notes: Shares the coarse filter paper's box; only the grade band is blue. filtering 2 because the ashless paper filters finer than the coarse grade.

name: Crated cracking reactor
description: A laboratory cracking reactor taken apart with care and strapped to a pallet: column, riser, separator, pipe spools and controller. Put back together and wired to power, it breaks heavy oils down into lighter fuels.
notes: On a 1.2 by 1.0 m pine pallet, 0.58 m high: a 1 m flanged column section with two bands, a riser pipe, a cyclone with its cone, three pipe spools, a cream controller cabinet with a screen and warning tag, and two straps over the load. Reassembling it into a standing machine needs a construction or furniture with a workstation, which has no content yet, so it is a plain item here. It needs lifting gear or a vehicle. The size is a placeholder.

name: Makeshift water electrolyser
description: A bolted steel tank of caustic solution on an angle-iron stand, with power terminals on its lid and two clear bubbler columns that keep the hydrogen and oxygen apart. It splits water into the two gases, slowly and at a heavy cost in power.
notes: A 600 by 360 by 400 mm tank on a stand, 1 m tall to the bubbler outlets: bolted lid, filler cap, gauge, red and black terminals with leads down to the floor, two clear columns half filled with water, red and blue tags and blue outlet hoses. The tiles draw the columns opaque. The columns and stand stretch the box. electrolysis is the quality name the electrolysis kit introduces, at a higher level since this one makes gas in bulk. It works where it stands, so it carries the quality as a workstation only. The size is a placeholder.

name: Stirling engine kit
description: A tabletop hot-air engine built from a kit: a glass cylinder over a small spirit burner drives a brass flywheel. It shows how heat can be turned into motion, and its parts are good for small mechanical projects.
notes: Assembled on a 220 by 120 mm dark steel base, 154 mm tall: a glass displacer cylinder with a steel displacer inside, a spirit burner and wick beneath, a brass power cylinder, linkage rods and a spoked flywheel 110 mm across. Modelled built rather than boxed, so it reads at a glance.

name: Makerspace building kit
description: A plastic case of gears, perforated beams, wheels, connector pegs and syringes with tubing for simple hydraulics, with a stack of blueprints for beginner building projects.
notes: A grey case 240 by 150 mm and 50 mm deep, its frosted lid hinged up behind: six compartments holding red and yellow gears, blue beams with holes, two syringes with blue tubing, two wheels, coloured pegs and a stack of blue blueprints. The raised lid triples the box.

name: Robotics building kit
description: A storage tub of snap-together parts, motors, sensors and a programmable controller brick, with a small two-wheeled robot built from it riding on the lid.
notes: A grey tub 280 by 190 mm and 80 mm tall with a dark lid, orange latches and a label, and on the lid a robot facing +z: orange frame, white controller brick with a screen and red button, two motors and wheels, a rear caster and steel ultrasonic eyes. The built robot shows what the tub is. The robot on top and the tub are both counted. Salvaging motors and the controller would come from disassembly, which has no draft field.

name: Hair hygroscope
description: A flat wooden wall board with a glazed window, behind which a single stretched hair lengthens and shrinks with the damp in the air, turning the needle on a dial at the top.
notes: A flat walnut wall board 120 mm wide, 400 mm tall and 20 mm deep with a hanging ring and no cornice or plinth, so it reads as a wall instrument rather than a clock, front on +z: a brass-bezelled white dial with ticks and a black needle, a wide brass-framed cream window with a dark hair, pulley, white tick scale and blued coil spring in contrast. humidity_measurement is the quality name the dial hygrometer introduces.

name: Ketene lamp
description: A length of glass pipe swelling into a bulb that holds an electric heating coil. Vapour run through it is cracked by the heat into gases too unstable to keep, so they must be fed straight into the next reaction.
notes: A 460 mm glass pipe 25 mm across with frosted ground joints at both ends and a 100 mm bulb in the middle holding a copper coil, a white socket on the bulb with a cable to a plug, resting on two white cradles. The tiles draw the glass opaque, hiding the coil. pyrolysis is a new quality name for cracking a vapour by heat. The cable, plug and cradles spread the box.
